text:
maria: FYI a customer (acct: brightcall) is seeing a surge of 504s and timeouts -> they report 95th p99 tail latency spikes during peak windows. started ~08:10 UTC. headers: x-tenant: brightcall, request-id: r-9f3a.
ashwin: can you paste the request path and example payload? suspect continuous batching backlog or queue depth exhaustion.
support-esc: copied from customer: POST /v1/generate
{"input":"long prompt... repeated calls at ~120 qps per tenant"}
They say it was fine yesterday, ramped up after a marketing push.
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-2812345670. Pager notified oncall.
jordan: checking gateway logs for tenant=brightcall now. seeing a lot of early-rejects? grep output:
```
2026-03-15T08:11:23Z gateway INFO reject early: queue_full tenant=brightcall queue_len=1024 max=1024
2026-03-15T08:11:24Z gateway WARN tail_latency spike p95=2.3s p99=9.8s
```
infra-sre: that max=1024 is the global per-shard queue cap. continuous-batcher backlog can fill KV cache warmups and block dequeue.
maria: customer provided a few request-ids: r-9f3a, r-9f4b, r-9f7c. all returned 504 gateway errors. They asked for repro steps to show to their SRE.
ashwin: short repro we used: run a script that sends concurrent requests with varied seq lengths to the hosted endpoint, keep open connections. we're able to reproduce p99 > 8s and some 504s within 2-3 minutes.
support-esc: mitigation suggested to customer: reduce concurrency to 40 qps, add retry jitter, and temporarily pin to a smaller model. they pushed back and asked for internal mitigation.
jordan: quick internal mitigation: increase per-shard queue cap from 1024->2048 for the region serving brightcall and add tenant rate-limiter overrides for their org. doing a staged change on shard-12 now.
oncall-bot: Change request submitted: CR-2026-8987 by jordan. ETA 3m.
infra-sre: note: increasing queue cap reduces early-rejects but may increase batching backlog and memory pressure on batchers; watch kv-cache warmups and host OOMs.
ashwin: disable continuous batching for tenant brightcall as a short-term bandaid — forces direct scheduling and reduces head-of-line blocking from long sequences. command applied: `tenantctl set-config brightcall continuous_batching false`.
maria: customer confirms 504s dropping after ~90s. they're seeing lower tail latency now. :relieved:
jordan: monitoring: p99 dropped from 9.8s -> 1.2s and early_rejects -> 0 within 4m. still watching for CPU spikes on batcher nodes.
infra-sre: opened follow-up action: tune per-tenant queue heuristics + autoscale batcher pools based on queue depth. assigning to eng-runtime for a permanent fix.
ashwin: eng-runtime, tagging you for follow-up: look at smarter dequeue prioritization (shortest-first or prompt-length-aware batching) and per-tenant soft-limits to avoid single-tenant starvation.
support-esc: I'll send the customer a postmortem summary and the temporary config changes we made, plus suggested client retry/backoff guidance.
maria: thanks everyone. closing incident when 24h stable. adding notes to ticket INC-2026-2812345670.
